cell_content.comparison: NFKC+casefold whitespace-insensitive ordered character sequence, compared by ordered alignment over nonempty matched-table cells; punctuation including numeric separators is retained.

frequency_association.comparison: Ordered source-table frequency/reaction associations; reaction word order and clinically meaningful qualifiers are preserved.

column_frequency_association.applicability: A positive source reaction/column/frequency association is required when the layout supports mapping; otherwise a positive row-frequency oracle must pass. Empty 0/0 comparisons never pass.

comparison_schema.candidate: Rust JSON pages[*].tables[*].{bbox_pt,rows[*].cells[*],lines}; cell text/bold/bboxes and flattened lines are read directly from Rust output.
comparison_schema.reference_table_detection: PyMuPDF page.find_tables() on Python-selected first-copy SmPC 4.8 pages, with per-document source-reviewed table adjudications and pinned-source fixtures where PyMuPDF has no reliable table.
comparison_schema.reference_cells: Raw PyMuPDF Table.extract() cells are retained for the raw comparison; adjudicated scoring adds only manually transcribed pinned-source fixture cells and excludes individually documented false detections.
comparison_schema.reference_flattening: The existing production flatten_table_rows() is applied to raw PyMuPDF reference cells only; source fixture rows are explicitly transcribed from the pinned PDF. Neither path uses native candidate cells.
comparison_schema.reference_frequency_associations: When the source layout requires manual association adjudication, reaction/frequency pairs are transcribed from pinned source cells with per-association source provenance; no expected pair is derived from native output.
comparison_schema.native_flattening: Native candidate flattened lines and rows are read directly from Rust output; Python does not rebuild them from native cells.
comparison_schema.table_identity: One-to-one greedy matching of candidate/reference bbox IoU on the same page; geometry is comparison-only and does not construct candidate rows.
comparison_schema.row_identity: NFKC+casefold, whitespace-collapsed exact line multiset; reported as a diagnostic.
comparison_schema.frequency_identity: Whitespace-insensitive ordered source-table reaction text units keyed by normalized frequency; reaction order, punctuation, and clinical qualifiers are preserved.
comparison_schema.column_frequency_identity: Whitespace-insensitive ordered reaction text units, physical frequency/assignment column, and frequency label are compared on matched tables. Applicability requires a positive reference mapping or a positive row-frequency alternate oracle.

selection.python_reference: The existing Python production extract_lines/split_sections/first_copy_headings/_table_owner_pages implementation selects first-copy SmPC 4.8 owner pages. This is explicitly the reference selection, not a Rust page-selection result.
selection.native_candidates: Only native tables on those Python-selected 4.8 pages are scored; native tables outside them are counted separately.

explicit_limits: The Python production parser selects section 4.8 pages and its first copy; this experiment does not measure native section-heading or repeated-copy selection.
Raw PyMuPDF comparisons remain unchanged and are reported alongside source-adjudicated comparisons; source fixtures are manual pinned-PDF transcriptions with page/hash/provenance.

Cell content uses whitespace-insensitive ordered character alignment (including punctuation); frequency and column gates preserve reaction order/qualifiers, require positive source evidence, and allow zero column assignments only when a positive alternate row oracle passes.
Bbox IoU measures table detection agreement, not semantic equivalence; different but useful table boundaries can reduce detection scores.
The reviewed bilingual oracles cover selected Eliquis Table 3 rows, not every adverse reaction, indication column, or table layout in the selected PDFs.
